summary: A dusthana lord in the house of loss: Sarala yoga in Phaladeepika and Raman's definition. Raman (with the 12th lord) calls it a Raja yoga that can bring religious learning and authority, Bhavartha Ratnakara says diseases are destroyed under certain conditions, and Braha calls it a 'moksha lord in a moksha house'; BPHS and Braha also read heavy expenses and a traditional longevity caution.
common_outcomes: A strong spiritual nature; meditation and renunciation (Braha); religious learning and piety when the 12th lord is well placed (Raman)
Unexpected expenditure, debts and losses (Raman; Braha; BPHS 24.96)
Difficulties tend to be absorbed: Raman's Raja yoga, Phaladeepika's Sarala yoga
rare_outcomes: BPHS 24.96: spends on evil deeds; a shortened life, more so with a malefic in the 12th (traditional view, never stated as a prediction)
Raman: benefics joining the 8th lord here give unfavourable results, including treachery of friends; with the 12th lord in a kendra or trikona, a seat of authority is thrust on the native
Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.7: the 8th lord in the 12th with debilitated or inimical planets and a strong lagna lord destroys all diseases
Raman, afflicted: secret vices (traditional view); Braha: troubles in foreign countries

by_area.personality: Fearless and resolute (Phaladeepika 6.65). Raman's 'clandestine acts' line is a traditional view tied to malefic affliction.
by_area.career: Raman: a post or seat of authority may be thrust on the native when the 12th lord is in a kendra or trikona.
by_area.finance: Unexpected expenditure and pecuniary losses (Raman); many expenses and debts (Braha); spending on evil deeds (BPHS 24.96).
by_area.health: Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.7: under the stated conditions diseases are destroyed; Braha lists left ear, left eye and anal complaints (traditional notes only).
by_area.relationships: Raman: treachery of friends when benefics join; Braha: no money from the marriage partner, little sexual strength.
by_area.spirituality: A moksha lord in a moksha house: strong spiritual nature, meditation, asceticism (Braha); religious learning and piety (Raman).

Raman: results must be modified by the strength of the lagna, the Moon and the running dasha; for indications of wrong conduct, a strong lagna, Moon and 10th mean the temptation is overcome (How to Judge a Horoscope p. 207)
lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15; Frawley; Braha): BPHS says the 8th lord is not auspicious, being 12th from the 9th; co-owning the 3rd, 7th or 11th makes it specifically harmful, co-owning a trikona makes it auspicious, and the Sun or Moon as 8th lord is not evil (Raman: neutral). Frawley calls the 2nd, 8th and 12th lords functionally neutral but the stain of the 8th the greatest; Braha warns that despite the sages' neutral rating a dusthana lord carries the most malefic energy. By lagna: Mars (1+8) is helpful for Aries (BPHS 34.19; Raman: benefic) and Venus (1+8) neutral for Libra (BPHS 34.33), and as lagna lords both stay generally auspicious (Frawley). Specifically harmful: Jupiter (8+11) for Taurus, Saturn (7+8) for Cancer, Mars (3+8) for Virgo, Mercury (8+11) for Scorpio, Venus (3+8) for Pisces. With a trikona: Saturn (8+9) for Gemini gives more good than bad because its mulatrikona rules the 9th (Frawley); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29, neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius is mixed (BPHS 34.41). The Moon (Sagittarius) and Sun (Capricorn) as 8th lords are neutral (BPHS 34.7, 34.39; Raman).

disagreements: Direct conflict on longevity: BPHS 24.96 and Braha read a short life, Phaladeepika 6.65 (Sarala) a long one; Bhavartha Ratnakara 5.7 reads freedom from disease under stated conditions. Raman agrees with Rath that benefics spoil this combination, and doubts Sarala's full results in practice.
